clue.text: Admit head has left college

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and here that letter has gone away

parts.note: to let on is to admit or confess something

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the principal has walked out of the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' gives LET ON; 'head has left' drops its first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is the famous English public school, formally Eton College, near Windsor.

clue.text: Left to throw up round ball: it's low in the air

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is thrown upwards, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
O is round in shape
a ball is a sphere

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to be sick around a ball game, feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, where weather happens.

clue.text: With no rival, I could be no plainer

indicators.note: the letters could be put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A boast: nobody could beat me, and I could not be any simpler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the speaker, the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, unrivalled, peerless.

clue.text: Having reconnoitred round college, I questioned systematically

indicators.note: one word is wrapped round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to case a place is to reconnoitre it before a crime, so having done so is cased
a tech is a technical college

explanation.surface: A spy who scouted a campus then interrogated someone methodically.
explanation.walkthrough: To case a joint is criminal slang for scouting it before a robbery; a tech is a technical college.
explanation.definitionFit: To catechise is to instruct or interrogate by a fixed series of questions and answers, as in religious teaching.

clue.text: Puma, say, mountain animal originally seen in tree

parts.note: the puma is a kind of big cat
an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: just the first letter of the word animal

explanation.surface: A mountain lion spotted up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is an ornamental tree with large heart-shaped leaves and long bean-like pods.

clue.text: Who, when intimate, resorted to a mystery story

indicators.note: re-sorted, put into order again, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Who, getting cosy, turns to a detective story.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins's 1859 sensation novel is an early classic of mystery fiction.

clue.text: Appear to be holding container for fruit dish

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: to come is to appear, turn up
a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A bowl seems to have a fruit pudding in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Compote is fruit stewed in syrup, served as a dessert.

clue.text: Burst of hail almost over

indicators.note: almost all the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: salve is a Latin greeting meaning hail
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A hailstorm nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous burst of gunfire, or a sudden burst of applause.

clue.text: Being imprisoned by magistrate, day to avoid

indicators.note: one letter is locked up inside the official

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice

explanation.surface: Someone jailed by a magistrate wants a day out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade or escape something by quick movement or trickery.

clue.text: With current having failed, right to probe old energy source?

parts.note: a computer system that has failed is down

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, as a probe goes inside

parts.note: steam powered engines of an earlier age

explanation.surface: An engineer, the power having failed, wonders about going back to steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' reads as electricity in the surface, but it is the flow of a river; 'to probe' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downstream means moving in the same direction as the flow of a river.

clue.text: Lump of fish, line caught

indicators.note: the fish has trapped the line inside it, as a fish takes a hook

parts.note: cod is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler lands a hefty fish that has swallowed the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a lump of earth or clay; the word also means an oaf.

clue.text: Botched delivery — baby not crying, do we hear?

indicators.note: the question asks whether these words sound like something said aloud

parts.note: a baby that is not crying gives no bawl

explanation.surface: A midwife's bungled delivery: the newborn is silent.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no ball is an illegal delivery by the bowler, penalised with an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an illegal bowling action or overstepping the crease produces a faulty delivery, called by the umpire.

clue.text: I wish I could manage to hold small lighter in canal

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letter for small within it

parts.note: 'Oh to' expresses a wish, as in 'Oh to be in England', written O TO
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Someone longs to grip a tiny lamp while in a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's otoscope shines a light into the ear canal for examination.

clue.text: I don't know foreign currency — let someone else deal with it

definitions.text: let someone else deal with it

parts.note: a quiz contestant who doesn't know says 'pass'
the buck is slang for the American dollar, a currency foreign to Britain

explanation.surface: Puzzled by overseas money, someone hands the problem to another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let someone else deal with it' is the definition; the clue's first half is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from a poker marker passed to the next dealer, means shirking a responsibility.

clue.text: Primate holding service initially in part of church

indicators.note: the primate's name contains the letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word service is taken

explanation.surface: A monkey in a church during the opening of a service.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: The samurai turn out to be rather incompetent

indicators.note: the letters turn out differently, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The famed warriors prove to be bunglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work is unskilled, like that of a beginner rather than a professional.

clue.text: Judge church house initially lacking somewhere to eat

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game

indicators.note: the word is missing its first letter

parts.note: a rectory is the house of a parish rector

explanation.surface: A judge says the vicarage first needs a dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is the dining hall of a monastery, college or school.

clue.text: Swerve left in running away

indicators.note: the letter for left sits in the other word

parts.note: a defection is a desertion, running away to the other side

explanation.surface: A fugitive veers to the left while fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A deflection is a turning aside from a course, as a ball deflects off a player.

clue.text: I'm ready for a row, caught by authoritative statement

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letter sits beside the word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an oracle is an authoritative pronouncement

explanation.surface: Someone spoiling for an argument after being caught out by an official declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker and hide, rowed with a paddle.

clue.text: I don't agree with old soldier? That's fine

parts.note: no is a word of disagreement
an old sweat is a veteran soldier

explanation.surface: An exchange of disagreement with a veteran, which ends amicably.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means no trouble at all, a reassurance that something is easy.

clue.text: Starts companion in suits

definitions.meaning: the word that partners starts in the phrase 'by ... and starts'
suits as a verb means is the right size or shape for

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a partner in a firm of lawyers or a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Fits pairs with starts in the idiom for irregular bursts, and fits is a synonym of suits.

clue.text: Terminal choice here, where the condemned are getting a new leader

indicators.note: the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: prisoners awaiting execution are held on death row

explanation.surface: Prisoners awaiting execution receive a fresh governor.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the first letter of DEATH ROW, is swapped for H. Heathrow is London's main airport, with several terminals to choose from.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main airport has five numbered terminal buildings, so a traveller picks one there.

clue.text: One not free to work everything, except at the start

indicators.note: everything apart from the first letter is used

parts.note: the lot means everything

explanation.surface: A labourer is busy all day except at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta, a forced labourer without freedom.

clue.text: Not like admirals in Whitehall to be disorganised

definitions.meaning: admirals in London's government offices are ashore, not out on the ocean

explanation.surface: Desk-bound naval chiefs in government are chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries, including the old Admiralty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is literally sailing the ocean, and figuratively being confused or bewildered.

clue.text: Holy Land area within borders of sand

indicators.note: the measure of land sits inside the outer letters
the outside letters of the word sand are taken

parts.note: an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: The Holy Land, a stretch of desert, edged with sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred describes something consecrated or venerated, set apart for worship.

clue.text: Stroke part of eye

definitions.meaning: an eyelash, one of the hairs on the eyelid

explanation.surface: A medical note: a stroke has affected part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash is both a blow with a whip and one of the hairs fringing the eyelid.

clue.text: Last month, courier moving around making heartfelt complaint

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the month
the letters of the word courier move into a new order

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: Last month a courier on the move made a sincere grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the courier's letters to CRIOEUR, which goes 'around' the month; the answer is a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'cry of the heart', a passionate protest or appeal.

clue.text: Participating in series of races is torture, yet one is running

indicators.note: the pieces take part inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy, is a series of motorcycle races
the rack is an instrument of torture
even is used to mean yet, as in 'even better'

explanation.surface: Taking part in a race series is agony, yet one keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race series; 'Participating in' puts the other pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A track event is an athletics race run on the track, such as the 400 metres.

clue.text: Big beasts pronounce about arresting king

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the letter, as police hold an arrested man
the word turns about, read backwards

parts.note: to pronounce is to say
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone declares that large animals have seized the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaks are large, shaggy wild or domesticated oxen of the Himalayas and Tibet.
